result.title: OrangeTree: A Linear and Tree-based Time Series Forecasting Model Supporting Multiple Input and Output Lengths
result.summary: Time series forecasting (TSF) models suffer from a critical rigidity: the inability to handle Multiple Input and Output Lengths (MIOL) within a single architecture. Current workarounds, such as padding or autoregression, often incur computational redundancy or suffer from error accumulation. We propose OrangeTree, a linear and tree-based architecture that decouples model parameters from sequence lengths. It employs a Segment Tree Encoder and an Inverse Tree Decoder to translate multi-length input history into multi-length output predictions within a unified framework. Crucially, a Range Weighter and a Feature Fuser bridge these components, dynamically selecting and fusing relevant ranges into optimal contexts for forecasting. Experiments on six benchmarks confirm OrangeTree achieves the SOTA performance. In MIOL settings, it matches the accuracy of length-fixed models without substantial accuracy degradation or a substantial increase in inference latency typical of heuristic methods. Code is available at https://github.com/Tang-Yiqi/OrangeTree.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 OrangeTree，用线性与树结构使模型参数与序列长度解耦，由 Segment Tree Encoder 与 Inverse Tree Decoder 配合 Range Weighter 和 Feature Fuser，在单一架构内完成多输入、多输出长度的时间序列预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其与长度无关的树状编码和「动态选择并融合相关区段」的机制，可能为 LVR 中变长输入的 latent 状态聚合、证据筛选与长度泛化提供可核查的结构线索，但领域相隔较远，迁移价值需人工判断。
